meta.title: BedBoard: live bed board for hospitals
meta.description: A free, open-source live bed board for hospitals. Nurses update in two taps; the whole hospital sees it instantly.

hero.title: Know every free bed, right now.
hero.sub: A free, open-source live bed board for hospitals. Nurses update in two taps; the whole hospital sees it instantly.

demo.title: Try it: tap a bed
demo.hint: This is a demo. Tap any bed to move it to its next step. Nothing is saved.
demo.legend: Every status has a colour, an icon and a word.

problem.title: Phone calls to every ward. Whiteboards that are hours old. Patients waiting on trolleys.
problem.text: In most small and mid-size Indian hospitals, bed status lives on a whiteboard or register in each ward. To admit a patient, the casualty doctor or admission clerk phones wards one by one.
problem.quote: “There is no real-time updation going on.”
problem.quoteContext: In Mumbai in May 2020, hospitals turned patients away, and the city’s bed dashboard was criticised for not being updated in real time. The internal tracking system was not open to the public.

s1.title: Nurse taps a bed
s1.text: Two taps on a phone: admit, discharge, mark cleaned.

s2.title: Desk sees it
s2.text: Free beds by ward and type, live. Reserve one for the patient on the way.

s3.title: Housekeeping gets the job
s3.text: The moment a patient leaves, the bed appears on the cleaning list.

discharge.title: Discharged at 11, gone at 5?
discharge.text: A discharge on paper is not a free bed. BedBoard shows every step (summary, bill, medicines) and turns red when a patient has waited too long, so beds free up sooner.

features.title: Everything a ward needs, nothing it does not

findBed.title: Find a bed

reports.title: Reports

public.text: A public page with counts only, if you choose to turn it on.

privacy.title: Names stay inside the ward. Public view shows numbers only.
privacy.p1: Patient names are visible only to that ward’s staff, the admission desk and administrators.
privacy.p2: Every status change is recorded in an audit log.
privacy.p3: Patient details are anonymised after a retention period you choose.

install.intro: You need a computer with Docker (2 GB of memory is enough) on your hospital network.
install.s1: Copy the settings file, then set your own passwords in it
install.s3: Open it in a browser and create your administrator

faq.title: Questions
faq.a1: Yes. It is open source under the MIT licence. There are no fees and no paid services.
faq.a2: No. It runs on your hospital network. If a ward phone loses signal, its taps are saved on the phone and sent when it reconnects.
faq.q3: Does it work with our hospital information system?
faq.a3: Not yet. This version runs beside your existing system. A way for a HIS to push admissions, and standard health-data export, are planned.
faq.a4: One computer with 2 GB of memory running Docker, on the hospital network. Staff use the browser on their own phones.
